### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.2

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

I often feel frustrated because many mainstream models supported in Cherry Studio are text-only unimodal models (e.g., GLM-5.1) or have extremely limited, underperforming visual understanding capabilities. Currently, Cherry Studio only allows users to set one global active model for an entire conversation. When I upload image-based materials (such as academic charts, literature screenshots, data visualizations, and figure panels from research papers) for analysis, the selected unimodal model cannot parse, interpret, or extract valid information from the visual content at all, resulting in irrelevant, inaccurate, or completely invalid responses.
To handle multi-modal tasks properly, I have to manually switch the global conversation model to a multi-modal capable one every time I upload images, which is extremely cumbersome. Moreover, frequent model switching breaks the consistency of the conversation context and text interaction experience, as different models have distinct strengths in text generation, long context processing, and conversation style. This pain point is especially prominent in academic research and document processing scenarios, where I regularly need to analyze visual materials alongside ongoing text conversations.

### Desired Solution

I would like Cherry Studio to add an independent model configuration feature dedicated to multi-modal tasks, with the following core design:
Add a separate Dedicated Model for Multi-Modal Tasks option in the model settings panel. This allows users to configure two default models independently: one primary model for regular text-only conversations, and a specialized multi-modal model exclusively for processing tasks that include uploaded images, visual content in PDFs, or other vision-related inputs.
Implement automatic model routing logic: when a user uploads image materials or triggers a multi-modal task in a conversation, the system automatically routes the relevant inference requests to the pre-configured dedicated multi-modal model, with no need for the user to manually switch the global conversation model. All pure text interactions will continue to use the user's primary model to maintain a consistent conversation experience.
Add quality-of-life optimizations: clearly label which models support multi-modal/visual understanding capabilities in the model selection dropdown, to help users quickly filter and select appropriate models. Meanwhile, retain a manual override option for users to temporarily select a different multi-modal model for specific conversations, balancing ease of use and flexibility.
This feature will allow users to fully leverage the strengths of different models: using models with strong text generation and long context handling capabilities for daily text tasks, while using powerful specialized multi-modal models to process visual content. It will completely solve the pain point of unimodal models failing to understand uploaded materials, and significantly improve the experience and efficiency of multi-modal usage scenarios in Cherry Studio.

title: [Bug]: Symlink created by bun install -g points to claude.exe instead of native binary (macOS arm64)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v.19.2

### Bug Description

When installing @anthropic-ai/claude-code globally via Bun, the claude symlink is created pointing to bin/claude.exe (a shell script stub) instead of the platform-specific native binary from the @anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64 optional dependency. This results in a ENOENT or JavaScript parse error when attempting to run claude.

Environment
- OS: macOS (arm64 / Apple Silicon)
- Bun version: v1.3.1 (89fa0f34) - bundled with Cherry Studio
- Package: @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.118
- Install method: bun install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install via Bun: bun install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
2. Try to run: bun /path/to/bin/claude or execute the claude binary directly
3. Error occurs

### Expected Behavior

## Actual Behavior
The symlink created at ~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude points to:
~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude -> ../../node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe
The claude.exe file contains a shell script stub:

```
echo "Error: claude native binary not installed." >&2
exit 1
When Bun tries to execute this file, it attempts to parse it as JavaScript and fails with:
1 | echo "Error: claude native binary not installed." >&2
         ^
error: Expected ";" but found ""Error: claude native binary not installed.""
    at /Users/xaibael/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe:1:6
1 | echo "Error: claude native binary not installed." >&2
                                                      ^
error: Unexpected >
    at /Users/xaibael/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe:1:51
In other cases (after the bin directory was cleaned), attempting to run the symlink results in:
error: ENOENT reading "/Users/xaibael/.cherrystudio/bin/claude"
```

## Expected Behavior
The symlink should point to the native binary from the platform-specific optional dependency package:
~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude -> ~/.cherrystudio/install/cache/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64@2.1

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

## Workaround
Manually recreate the symlink to point to the correct native binary:
`rm ~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude`

`ln -s "~/.cherrystudio/install/cache/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64@2.1.118@@@1/claude" ~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude`

`chmod +x ~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude`


## Root Cause
It appears that Bun's global install resolves the bin entry from package.json and creates a symlink to bin/claude.exe, but does not correctly resolve the optional dependency (@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64) that the postinstall script or runtime would normally use to replace the stub with the native binary. The postinstall script (which copies the native binary into place) may not be running during Bun's global install, or the symlink is created before postinstall has a chance to run.

title: [Bug]:  Mistral Small 4 / mistral-small-2603 is missing vision and reasoning_effort support
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.2

### Bug Description

Mistral Small 4 (`mistral-small-2603`, also exposed through `mistral-small-latest`) supports image input and adjustable reasoning according to Mistral's official docs, but Cherry Studio's built-in Mistral provider does not seem to handle those capabilities correctly.

The two problems I ran into:

1. `mistral-small-2603` is not detected as a vision model by default, so image input is not available unless I manually edit the model and enable the Vision capability.

2. Mistral Small 4 supports adjustable reasoning through the `reasoning_effort` request parameter, but setting this as an assistant custom parameter under Cherry Studio's built-in `Providers -> Mistral` does not appear to enable thinking/reasoning.

I tested this on Windows with the built-in Mistral provider using a normal local Cherry Studio setup.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio.
2. Go to `Settings -> Providers -> Mistral`.
3. Configure the built-in Mistral provider.
4. Add or use the model `mistral-small-2603`.
5. Select this model in an assistant.
6. Try to attach/send an image.

Observed:
- Image input is not available by default for `mistral-small-2603`.

Then try to enable reasoning:

7. Open the assistant's model settings.
8. Add a custom parameter:
   - name: `reasoning_effort`
   - type: `string`
   - value: `high`
9. Send a normal chat request using `mistral-small-2603`.

Observed:
- The model does not appear to receive or apply Mistral's `reasoning_effort` setting.

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio's built-in Mistral provider should correctly support Mistral Small 4 capabilities:

- `mistral-small-2603` should be recognized as a vision-capable model.
- Image input should be available without manually overriding the model capability.
- The Mistral provider should support sending `reasoning_effort`, for example:
  - `reasoning_effort: "high"`
  - `reasoning_effort: "none"`

For Mistral's Chat Completions API, this parameter should be sent as part of the request body.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

Mistral docs:

- Mistral Small 4 announcement:
  https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-small-4

- Adjustable reasoning docs:
  https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/conversations/reasoning/adjustable

- Mistral chat endpoint docs:
  https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/chat

I did a quick read through Cherry Studio's source and I think this may be caused by two separate config/code-path issues.

For vision, the model detection appears to include older/current aliases such as `mistral-small-2506` and `mistral-small-latest`, but not the new explicit model id `mistral-small-2603`.

For reasoning, adding `reasoning_effort` as an assistant custom parameter does not seem to work with the built-in Mistral provider because Cherry routes built-in Mistral through the AI SDK Mistral provider. In that path, the custom parameter appears to be treated as a provider option, not necessarily as Mistral's top-level chat-completions request field.

In other words, I can add this in the UI:

```json
{
  "reasoning_effort": "high"
}

but with the built-in Mistral provider it does not look like Cherry sends it in the same way Mistral's API expects:

{
  "model": "mistral-small-2603",
  "messages": [...],
  "reasoning_effort": "high"
}

As a workaround, using an OpenAI-compatible/New API style provider pointed at Mistral may be able to pass the parameter, but the built-in `Providers -> Mistral` integration should ideally support this directly.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Every consumer that kicks off a translation (`TranslatePage`, `ActionTranslate`, `TranslateWindow`, the space-key auto-translate in `InputbarCore`, and potentially others) hand-rolls the same flow:

- call `translateText()`
- manage an `isTranslating` state
- suppress `isAbortError` on user-initiated cancels
- log the failure
- surface a toast with `formatErrorMessageWithPrefix`
- manage its own abort controller wiring

Because every consumer owns the boilerplate, they drift. Code review on PR #13871 caught `InputbarCore` and `TranslateWindow` independently mis-handling the same concerns (wrong log level, missing toast, no abort-error distinction), which each had to be patched in place. New translate entry points added in the future will repeat the drift.

### Desired Solution

Extract a single `useTranslate` hook that owns the translate flow end-to-end - the call, the loading state, the abort handling, and the standard error presentation - so each consumer just hands it input text and a target language.

Consumers that need custom behavior (e.g. a page that shows errors inline rather than as a toast) should be able to opt out of the default feedback via options, mirroring how `useMutationFeedback` works for the mutation hooks added earlier in this PR.

git log shows there used to be a `useTranslate` hook (`97af83c2f refactor: move useTranslate hook to translate module`) that has since been dissolved back into its consumers. This issue is asking to revive that direction with the benefit of hindsight.

### Alternative Solutions

Leaving the boilerplate duplicated and patching each consumer individually - current state, and what PR #13871's translate review threads made visible.

### Additional Information

Consumers that should migrate to the hook in the rollout:

- `src/renderer/src/pages/translate/TranslatePage.tsx`
- `src/renderer/src/windows/selection/action/components/ActionTranslate.tsx`
- `src/renderer/src/windows/quickAssistant/translate/TranslateWindow.tsx`

title: [Feature]: Build a shared selector composite in @cherrystudio/ui and AssistantSelectorV2 / AgentSelectorV2 wrappers on top of the v2 data/UI refactor
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-alpha

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

This request is built on top of the ongoing work on the `v2` branch and is the assistant/agent counterpart to #14483.

The background is the same: the v2 data refactor moves renderer-side data to the new data layer (consumed via DataApi-based hooks), and the UI refactor moves new components to the Shadcn + Tailwind direction under `@cherrystudio/ui`. New consumers - chiefly the `pages/library` editor flows, which are not allowed to reuse `AgentSettings` or `pages-agents` components - need a way to pick an assistant or an agent without each editor reinventing its own popup.

Continuing to extend the legacy pickers (`AddAssistantPopup`, the `pages-agents` sidebar, etc.) directly is expensive and cannot keep behavior fully aligned once the underlying data layer and UI conventions have changed. As with #14483, it makes more sense to introduce a v2-aligned standalone selector instead of patching the legacy ones in place.

### Desired Solution

Introduce **one shared presentational selector composite in `@cherrystudio/ui`** plus **two thin business wrappers in the renderer** built on top of it.

**1. Shared selector composite (in `@cherrystudio/ui`)** - fully presentational, no business or data-layer dependency. An audit of the current `@cherrystudio/ui` surface shows that the closest existing piece (`Combobox`, which already has multi-select + search + custom trigger) does not cover the required structure: it has no per-item left/right action slots, no sticky footer row, and no filter-toggle panel. Rather than overload `Combobox` with unrelated concerns, this should ship as a new composite layered on top of the existing `Popover` / `Command` / `Button` primitives. Layout the composite must support:

- a business-supplied `trigger` slot (any node)
- on click: a popover containing
  - **top row**: search input + a filter toggle button (the filter panel expands to show tag chips + sort dropdown)
  - a multi-select toolbar with a multi-select on/off toggle (whether multi-select is allowed is decided by the consumer via prop)
  - a vertically scrollable list with a max height; **each row exposes two action affordances**: left side (pin button + selected-state mark) and right side ("jump to detail config page")
  - a bottom sticky row with a single "create new" entry that always shows and jumps to the create page
- both single-select and multi-select modes (mode is a prop)

**2. `AssistantSelectorV2`** (renderer business wrapper) - wraps the shared composite with the assistant data source, the assistant tag filter (via the existing tag system), the assistant detail/create routes, and the assistant pinning preference key.

**3. `AgentSelectorV2`** (renderer business wrapper) - wraps the shared composite with the agent data source, the agent detail/create routes, and the agent pinning preference key. The tag filter is intentionally not included in the first cut; an agent tag filter is planned as a follow-up once agent data grows a tag concept.

Pinning is part of the v2 data design, aligned with the model pinning direction in #14483: pinned IDs should be stored in user Preference under v2 storage rather than as ad-hoc local UI state, so they persist across sessions and sync across windows.

The composite and the wrappers should follow the new Shadcn + Tailwind conventions; legacy UI patterns (antd, styled-components, ad-hoc popups) must not be introduced.

### Alternative Solutions

Continue modifying `AddAssistantPopup`, the `pages-agents` sidebar, and other legacy assistant/agent pickers in place, attempting to migrate them to the v2 data layer and UI stack while preserving their old internal structure.

This is cheaper short-term but raises long-term migration cost and makes it harder to align these pickers with the v2 data flow, UI conventions, and pinning storage model. It also leaves `@cherrystudio/ui` without a reusable selector composite, which means future selectors (e.g. the `ModelSelectorV2` proposed in #14483) cannot share the same primitive.

### Additional Information

- Scope: one shared presentational composite in `@cherrystudio/ui` + two renderer business wrappers (`AssistantSelectorV2`, `AgentSelectorV2`).
- The shared composite is intentionally placed in `@cherrystudio/ui` (rather than in the renderer next to the wrappers) so future selectors - including the `ModelSelectorV2` work in #14483 - can compose the same primitive instead of duplicating the structure.
- Tag filter: Assistant-only in this iteration; Agent tag filter is a planned follow-up.
- Pinning: aligned with #14483 - pinned IDs go into Preference.
- Out of scope: migrating existing legacy call sites; agent tag filter; full batch-operation UX in the multi-select toolbar (the toolbar slot itself is in scope, but specific batch actions are deferred to consumers).

title: [Bug]: Pre-commit hook skips oxlint, so CI-only lint failures slip through
body:

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Bug Description

The repository's pre-commit hook and the CI "Lint Check" step do not run the same set of linters, so lint failures show up in CI even when pre-commit passed locally.

The `Lint Check` job in `basic-checks` runs `pnpm lint`, whose script composition is:

```
oxlint --fix && eslint . --ext ... --fix --cache && pnpm typecheck && pnpm i18n:check && pnpm format
```

The pre-commit hook (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`) only runs ESLint on staged files; there is no oxlint step:

```yaml
- id: eslint-fix
  entry: pnpm eslint --fix
```

Rules that live in oxlint but aren't enforced by the project's ESLint config therefore pass pre-commit and break CI. A concrete case hit during PR #13871: oxlint's `typescript/consistent-type-imports` rejected an import in `_mutationFeedback.ts` that used `loggerService` only inside `typeof`; pre-commit's ESLint step accepted it, CI's `pnpm lint` failed.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Introduce a type-only import in a TS file written as a value import, e.g. `import { loggerService } from '@logger'` when `loggerService` is only referenced inside `typeof`.
2. Run `pnpm eslint --fix` (what pre-commit executes) - passes.
3. Run `pnpm lint` (what CI executes) - fails with `All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use \`import type\`.`

### Expected Behavior

Pre-commit catches anything that CI's `Lint Check` step would catch. Either:

- add an `oxlint-fix` hook before `eslint-fix` in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, or
- replace the current `eslint-fix` entry with `pnpm test:lint` (oxlint + eslint, aligned with the CI command), accepting the extra runtime cost.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
X Lint Check
...
X All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use `import type`.
basic-checks: src/renderer/src/hooks/translate/_mutationFeedback.ts#1
```

### Additional Context

Failing CI run (pre fix): https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/actions/runs/24837890810
Follow-up commit that patched it in-tree: 68f95adc6 (on PR #13871).

title: Make auto-i18n cover the v2 branch
body:
`.github/workflows/auto-i18n.yml` syncs locales nightly but its PR-creation step is hardcoded to `base: "main"` (line 88). Active v2 development lives on the `v2` branch, so any i18n key added during v2 work never gets its translations backfilled automatically - contributors must hand-run `pnpm i18n:sync` inside every feature PR that touches i18n or the `i18n Check` CI step will fail.

Hit this on PR #13871: a `translate.error.detect.failed` key added to `zh-cn` + `en-us` but missing in `zh-tw` (and the extra locales under `src/renderer/src/i18n/translate/*.json`) tripped CI until the sync was run manually.

## Desired

Auto-i18n should also cover `v2` while it's the active development line. Any of these shapes works:

- run the workflow as a matrix over `main` and `v2`, each creating its own sync PR against the corresponding base; or
- duplicate the workflow with `base: "v2"`; or
- expose a manual-dispatch input that picks the target branch on demand.

## Related

- Context PR: #13871
- Failing CI run: https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/actions/runs/24838046357

### Platform

Linux

### Version

v2 (dev branch)

### Bug Description

In V2 dark mode, the Code Tools page (`/app/code`) has severe visibility problems:

1. **CLI tool icons**: GitHub Copilot CLI and OpenCode icons use hardcoded `fill="#000"` in their SVG, making them invisible against dark backgrounds.
2. **Text elements nearly invisible**: Many Tailwind classes apply opacity modifiers (e.g. `/30`, `/40`, `/50`) on top of semantic color tokens that already have reduced opacity in dark mode (e.g. `--cs-foreground-muted` is `oklch(1 0 0 / 0.4)`). This double-opacity reduction makes text effectively 5-12% white - nearly invisible. Affected elements include:
   - Search bar background, border, and placeholder text
   - Tool count label
   - Field labels and info icons
   - Provider names in model dropdown
   - Section title in tool grid
   - Official badge text
   - Environment variables textarea border and placeholder
   - Auto-update checkbox label
   - Drawer footer summary text and separator dots
   - Tool card border and background

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Switch to dark mode
2. Navigate to Code Tools page (`/app/code`)
3. Observe that many text labels, borders, and icons are nearly invisible
4. Open any tool's launch configuration drawer - labels, info icons, and summary text are barely visible

### Expected Behavior

All text, icons, borders, and interactive elements should have sufficient contrast against the dark background to be clearly readable and usable.

### Additional Context

Root causes:
1. SVG icons with `fill="#000"` instead of `fill="currentColor"` - only affects `githubCopilotCli.tsx` and `openCode.tsx`; other CLI icons use brand colors correctly.
2. Double-opacity problem: dark mode semantic tokens already carry reduced opacity (~40% for muted text, ~10% for borders), and Tailwind opacity modifiers further halve them. Fix is to remove or reduce the extra opacity modifiers for dark-mode-appropriate values.

title: [Bug]: useInfiniteQuery's mutate type erases extra fields beyond CursorPaginationResponse<T>
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Bug Description

`useInfiniteQuery` in `src/renderer/src/data/hooks/useDataApi.ts` types its returned `mutate` as `KeyedMutator<CursorPaginationResponse<T>[]>`, where `T` is the item type inferred from `InferPaginatedItem<TPath>`.

This shape is wrong for any endpoint whose response **extends** `CursorPaginationResponse<T>` with extra top-level fields. The most concrete case in the codebase: `BranchMessagesResponse extends CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>` and adds `activeNodeId: string | null`.

When a consumer reads or writes pages via the returned `mutate`, the type system erases `activeNodeId` (and any other extras), so updater callbacks cannot read or modify the field without an unsafe cast.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open `src/renderer/src/data/hooks/useDataApi.ts` and look at `UseInfiniteQueryResult<T>` (around line 184) and the `useInfiniteQuery` function definition.
2. Note that the mutate field is typed `KeyedMutator<CursorPaginationResponse<T>[]>` - only the item type `T` flows through.
3. Try to consume it for a path whose schema declares `response: BranchMessagesResponse`:

```ts
const { mutate } = useInfiniteQuery('/topics/:topicId/messages', {
  params: { topicId },
  query: { includeSiblings: true },
  limit: 50
})

// Want to write a new pages array that preserves activeNodeId:
const refreshed: BranchMessagesResponse[] = await someFetch()
await mutate(refreshed)
//        ^^^^^^^^^
// Type error: BranchMessagesResponse[] is not assignable to
// CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>[].
//
// Workaround that consumers end up adopting:
//   mutate as unknown as KeyedMutator<BranchMessagesResponse[]>
// - defeats type safety, has to be repeated in every consumer.
```

### Expected Behavior

The hook should preserve the **full response type** declared in the path schema, not collapse it to `CursorPaginationResponse<T>`. `mutate`, and any cache-related fields, should be typed against the actual response shape so consumers can read/write top-level extras (`activeNodeId`, custom pagination metadata, etc.) without `unknown` casts.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
Type 'KeyedMutator<CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>[]>' is not assignable to type 'KeyedMutator<BranchMessagesResponse[]>'.
  Type 'CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>[]' is not comparable to type 'BranchMessagesResponse[]'.
    Property 'activeNodeId' is missing in type 'CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>' but required in type 'BranchMessagesResponse'.
```

### Additional Context

The pattern affects every path whose schema response is a `CursorPaginationResponse<T>` subtype. Today it's only `BranchMessagesResponse`, but any future paginated endpoint that wants to attach top-level metadata (`totalUnread`, `cursorMode`, `lastSyncTime`, etc.) hits the same wall.

The non-paginated read hook `useQuery` does not have this problem - it correctly types `data` as `ResponseForPath<TPath, 'GET'>`. Only `useInfiniteQuery` collapses the shape.

Instead, an "AI_APICallError: Invalid JSON response" error message appeared. ### Expected Behavior It is compatible with both URL and b64_json return formats. If the server returns a URL, the client can also parse and load the image correctly. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell ``` ### Additional Context Besides Zod validation failure, an `InvalidCharacterError: Failed to execute 'atob' on 'Window'` is also triggered when attempting to bypass or forcibly returning a URL by certain APIs. This is because the `convertBase64ToUint8Array` function attempts to decode the URL string returned by the API using `atob()`. title: Bug: MCP with Claude model fails due to invalid anthropic-beta header value `structured-outputs-2025-11-13`
body:
## Describe the Bug

When using Cherry Studio v1.9.3 with a Claude model and enabling MCP (Model Context Protocol), the request fails with an error about an invalid `anthropic-beta` header value.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Claude model (e.g., via Vertex AI / Anthropic API)
2. Enable MCP in Cherry Studio settings
3. Send any message / trigger MCP tool call
4. Error is returned immediately

## Expected Behavior

MCP should work normally with Claude models without header errors.

## Actual Behavior

The following error is returned (repeated twice):

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "message": "Unexpected value(s) \`structured-outputs-2025-11-13\` for the \`anthropic-beta\` header. Please consult our documentation at docs.anthropic.com or try again without the header."
  },
  "request_id": "req_vrtx_011CaTt9LEAvrJTcMDBDWasZ"
}
```

## Environment

- **Cherry Studio Version:** 1.9.3
- **Model Provider:** Claude (Vertex AI endpoint, based on request_id prefix `req_vrtx_`)
- **MCP:** Enabled

## Analysis

The app is sending `anthropic-beta: structured-outputs-2025-11-13` as a request header, but the Anthropic API (specifically the Vertex AI proxy endpoint) does not recognize this header value. This could be:

1. An outdated beta header value that has since been removed/renamed by Anthropic
2. A header value that is only valid for direct Anthropic API but not for Vertex AI proxy
3. Cherry Studio hardcoding a beta header that should be dynamically determined

## Suggested Fix

- Remove or update the `structured-outputs-2025-11-13` value from the `anthropic-beta` header
- Alternatively, only include the beta header when calling the direct Anthropic API, not when routing through Vertex AI

## Additional Context

This completely blocks MCP usage with Claude models in v1.9.3. Works fine when MCP is disabled.

title: Inconsistent ID generation for agents - agent_<timestamp>_<random> vs UUID in DB schema
body:
## Problem

The agent-related tables use inconsistent ID generation strategies:

### 1. `agentId` uses `agent_<timestamp>_<random>` instead of UUID

The DB table defines the ID as:
```ts
id: uuidPrimaryKey()
```

But in `createAgent(req: CreateAgentDto): Promise<AgentEntity>`:
```ts
const id = `agent_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 11)}`
```

This generates a string like `agent_1734567890123_x7k2m9p4q` which does **not** conform to UUID format, conflicting with the `uuidPrimaryKey()` schema definition.

### 2. `agentSession` table explicitly bypasses UUID

```ts
'agent_session',
{
  // IDs use the app-generated "session_<timestamp>_<random>" format, not UUIDs,
  // so uuidPrimaryKey() is intentionally not used here. Callers must always supply an id.
  id: text().primaryKey(),
}
```

This works, but it's inconsistent with other tables and the codebase-wide UUID convention.

### 3. Need full audit

All agent-related tables should be reviewed for ID generation consistency. Likely tables include:
- `agent`
- `agent_session`
- Any other agent-related junction or mapping tables

## Expected Behavior

All agent-related IDs should follow a single, consistent strategy - either:
- Use `uuidPrimaryKey()` everywhere and generate UUIDs in the app layer, or
- Explicitly use `text().primaryKey()` everywhere with the `agent_<timestamp>_<random>` pattern (but this breaks consistency with the rest of the codebase)

Given the rest of the codebase uses UUIDs, the first option seems preferable.

### Bug Description

When a non-multimodal model is configured for the Agent feature, the image attachment button in the input toolbar becomes unavailable or hidden. This restriction is unreasonable for the following reasons:

1. **Agents may only need to pass image files as attachments to tools** - the model itself doesn't need to understand the image content. For example, an Agent might process images through MCP tools, code execution, or other external services.
2. **Agents may use other tools to understand images**, such as calling OCR APIs, vision model APIs, etc. Restricting image uploads blocks these workflows entirely.
3. The purpose of image attachments should not be determined solely by the model's capabilities. It should be determined by the user and the Agent's toolchain.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Select a non-multimodal model (e.g., a text-only model)
2. Configure that model for the Agent feature
3. Open the Agent conversation interface
4. Try to add an image attachment via the input toolbar
5. Observe that the image upload button is unavailable or hidden

### Expected Behavior

The input toolbar in Agent mode should allow users to add image attachments regardless of whether the model supports multimodal input. The model's vision capability should not be the deciding factor for attachment uploads, as Agents can process images through other means (tool calls, file passing, external APIs, etc.).

### Relevant Log Output

_No relevant logs_

### Additional Context

This issue specifically affects Agent mode. The restriction appears to be overly aggressive - while it makes sense to limit image uploads for non-multimodal models in regular chat mode (where the model must directly process the image), Agent mode fundamentally changes the paradigm by introducing a tool-using layer between the user's input and the model's processing.

When using **deepseek-v4-pro** model in the **default assistant on the home page**, the assistant stays in an infinite loading state and eventually causes the renderer process to crash.

The root cause appears to be that deepseek-v4-pro outputs `thinking` type content blocks (chain-of-thought reasoning tokens) which the standard chat UI does not handle. This leads to:

1. Warning logs: `Unhandled assistant content block type: thinking`
2. Warning logs: `Received content_block_stop for unknown index`
3. Eventually: `Renderer process crashed with: {"reason":"crashed","exitCode":-1073741819}`

**Note**: The same model works correctly in Agent mode (Claude Code SDK agent), suggesting the issue is specific to the standard chat UI's handling of `thinking` content blocks.

Additionally, the default assistant preset appears to be corrupted:
- `Assistant preset with id default not found in state` - repeated multiple times after restart

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Cherry Studio v1.9.3 on Windows
2. Configure a valid DeepSeek API key in Settings -> Provider -> DeepSeek
3. Fetch model list and select `deepseek-v4-pro` in the default assistant
4. Send any message to the default assistant
5. The assistant shows infinite loading with no response
6. After 5-10 minutes, the renderer process crashes completely
7. After restart, the issue persists - default assistant still cannot be used

### Expected Behavior

1. The standard chat UI should correctly handle `thinking` type content blocks from reasoning models (either display them appropriately or safely ignore them)
2. The renderer process should not crash when receiving unsupported content block types
3. The default assistant preset should persist after restart

### Relevant Log Output

```
{"level":"warn","message":"Unhandled assistant content block","timestamp":"...","type":"thinking"}
{"index":1,"level":"warn","message":"Received content_block_stop for unknown index","timestamp":"..."}
{"level":"error","message":"Renderer process crashed with: {\"reason\":\"crashed\",\"exitCode\":-1073741819}","module":"WindowService","process":"main","timestamp":"..."}
{"level":"warn","message":"Assistant preset with id default not found in state.","module":"useAssistantPresets","process":"renderer","timestamp":"..."}
```

### Additional Context

- The issue does NOT occur with non-reasoning models (e.g., deepseek-chat)
- The Agent (Cherry Assistant) works fine with deepseek-v4-pro since the Claude Code SDK handles thinking blocks correctly
- The error log file is at `%APPDATA%/CherryStudio/logs/app-error.YYYY-MM-DD.log`

- **Platform**: Windows
- **Version**: v1.9.4

### Bug Description

When using the **DeepSeek Official API** (api.deepseek.com) provider with the `deepseek-v4` model, typing `/context` shows the context length as **200K**. However, DeepSeek officially announced that V4 supports up to **1M** context length (1,000,000 tokens).

This discrepancy means users may not be aware that they can leverage the full 1M context window that DeepSeek V4 actually supports.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio v1.9.4 on Windows 11
2. Add DeepSeek Official API provider (api.deepseek.com)
3. Select the `deepseek-v4` model and start a conversation
4. Type `/context` in the chat input
5. The displayed context length is **200K** instead of the expected **1M**

### Expected Behavior

The `deepseek-v4` model should show **1M (1,000,000 tokens)** as its context length when queried via `/context`, matching DeepSeek's official specification.

### Additional Context

Looking at the Cherry Studio model definitions, `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` are pre-configured with 64K context length. The `deepseek-v4` model may be inheriting a default value of 200K from the backend model list (api.cherry-ai.com) rather than its actual 1M cap. The model metadata for `deepseek-v4` needs to be updated to reflect the correct context length.

Note: The thinking mode toggle support for DeepSeek V4 has been requested in multiple issues (#14553, #14576, #14664, #14670, #14673) and is presumably already being worked on. This issue focuses specifically on the context length configuration.

This is part of the ongoing v2 UI migration away from legacy antd and styled-components usage. The current shared renderer component area still carries many legacy UI dependencies even though the target UI stack is `@cherrystudio/ui` + Tailwind CSS.

Inventory was taken from `src/renderer/src/components` only on 2026-05-07:

- #14297 generic Drawer / Code Tool v2 design work
- #14535 shared selector composite work
- #14339 / #14351 translate-page UI work

Replace the remaining antd and styled-components usage under `src/renderer/src/components` with repo-standard primitives and styling:

- Prefer existing `@cherrystudio/ui` primitives/composites before adding new local wrappers.
- Use Tailwind CSS and Cherry Studio design tokens instead of `styled-components` for presentation styles.

title: [Feature]: Bundle Portable Runtimes (uv, Git, Node) into Installer to Eliminate Environment Dependencies
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio depends on three external runtimes - uv, Git, and Node.js - but none of them ship with the installer. Users must download or install them separately, and each one has its own failure mode:

- **uv**: Downloaded at runtime via `install-uv.js` from a gitcode.com mirror with a hardcoded version. Frequently fails behind corporate firewalls, on weak networks, or offline - users see repeated "please install uv" prompts and MCP servers that depend on `uvx` simply don't work.
- **Git**: On macOS, `/usr/bin/git` is an Xcode CLT shim that passes the app's availability check but fails on actual `git clone`. On Windows, users must manually install Git for Windows and configure `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH`; those using fnm/nvm/mise find their PATH ignored by Git Bash.
- **Node.js**: Required for `npx`-based MCP servers. Non-developer users rarely have it installed. The current fallback to bundled `bun` has compatibility gaps (`.cmd` shims rejected on Windows, argument translation issues).

The combined effect: a non-developer user who installs Cherry Studio and tries to use Agent mode or MCP servers hits a wall of cryptic errors about missing tools they've never heard of.

## Goal

After installing Cherry Studio, all runtime-dependent features (MCP servers, Agent mode, skills, OpenClaw) work out of the box - the installer bundles portable uv, Git, and Node.js binaries so users never need to install developer tools or configure PATH manually.

## Spec

- The installer includes platform-specific portable binaries for uv, Git, and Node.js for each supported platform (macOS arm64/x64, Windows x64, Linux x64/arm64).
- On first launch, bundled binaries are extracted to the app's local binary directory and added to the app's internal PATH - no user action required.
- System-first priority: if the user already has a working system-installed version (meeting minimum version requirements), the system version takes priority over the bundled one.
- The runtime download scripts (`install-uv.js`, `install-bun.js`) and their associated UI prompts ("please install uv/bun") are removed; required tools are always present after install.
- Bundled binary versions are updated as part of the regular release process, not hardcoded in download scripts.
- On macOS, the bundled Git replaces reliance on the Xcode CLT shim - the app no longer assumes `/usr/bin/git` works.
- On Windows, the bundled Git includes git-bash, eliminating the need for users to install Git for Windows or set `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH`.
- The bundled Node.js provides `npx` directly, removing the bun-based npx fallback and its compatibility issues.
- All bundled binaries run in an isolated environment scoped to Cherry Studio - they do not modify the user's global PATH, shell profile, or system-level configuration.
- Phased delivery: uv ships first (P0, smaller binary ~12 MB, lower complexity); Git and Node.js follow in a subsequent release (larger binaries, platform-specific packaging complexity).

## Verification

- **[uv] Fresh install, offline**: macOS arm64, disconnect network before first launch, activate an MCP server requiring `uvx` - it should start successfully using bundled uv, no "install uv" dialog appears.
- **[uv] System uv present**: User has system uv 1.2.0 installed - Cherry Studio detects and uses the system version, not the bundled one (verify via version in logs).
- **[uv] Upgrade path**: Upgrade from a version that used `install-uv.js` to this version - no download prompt appears; previously downloaded uv in `~/.cherrystudio/bin` still works if newer than bundled.
- **[Git] macOS without Xcode CLT**: Fresh macOS with no Xcode CLT installed, use Agent mode that calls `git clone` - should succeed using bundled Git, no Xcode installation popup.
- **[Git] Windows without Git for Windows**: Fresh Windows install with no Git, enter Agent mode - should work without "Git Bash not found" error, no need to set `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH`.
- **[Node] No system Node**: Fresh install with no system Node.js, activate an MCP server specified with `npx` command - should start successfully using bundled Node/npx, not fall back to bun.
- **[Node] Windows .cmd shim**: Windows user with Node installed via fnm - MCP servers using `npx` should work regardless of `.cmd` shim issues, since bundled Node provides a real `npx` binary.
- **[Isolation] No global pollution**: After install and use, user's global PATH, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`, and Windows system PATH remain unmodified by Cherry Studio's bundled binaries.
- **[Size] Installer growth**: Per-platform installer size increase stays within reasonable bounds (uv phase: <15 MB; full bundle phase: <150 MB).
- **[Priority override] System version wins**: User with Node 22 installed globally, Cherry Studio bundles Node 20 - app uses the system Node 22, not the older bundled one.

title: [Feature]: Cherry Studio Account System and Cross-Device Data Sync
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio currently has no first-party account system. Users who work across multiple devices (e.g. office Windows + home Mac) rely on WebDAV or S3 full-backup-and-restore to move data between machines. This approach suffers from frequent data overwrites when multiple clients back up to the same path (#1793), restoration failures when backup files exceed 512 MB (#12072), inability to merge changes from different devices (#10835), and the general friction of manually triggering backup/restore cycles. Users have repeatedly asked for account-based sync that "just works" (#12663 #10982 #12483 #12493), but no solution exists today. Meanwhile, Cherry Studio needs an account foundation to support upcoming value-added services - cloud storage, cloud VM, model services, and a credits system.

## Goal

Users can register a Cherry Studio account, log in across devices, and keep all their data - conversations, assistants, settings, API keys, and knowledge base - automatically synchronized, with an open-source sync server that can be self-hosted.

## Spec

- **Account system (Passport)**: Users can register and log in to a Cherry Studio account via the client. The Passport service first launches as a standalone web service (Express), then integrates into the desktop and mobile clients.
- **Credits and value-added services**: Each account has a credits balance. Credits unlock value-added services: cloud storage quota, cloud VM access, model API services, and model tools.
- **Full-scope sync**: After login, the following data categories sync across devices: conversations (topics + messages), assistant configurations, model provider and API key settings, app settings (general, display, data), and knowledge base entries.
- **Opt-in conversation cloud sync**: Conversation content upload to Cherry Studio's cloud is off by default. Users explicitly enable it in settings. When disabled, only configuration and metadata sync; conversations stay local.
- **Open-source sync server**: The multi-device sync server is released as an open-source project. Users who prefer to control their own data can deploy it on their own VPS and point their clients to it.
- **Incremental sync with conflict resolution**: Sync operates incrementally - only changed records are transmitted. When the same record is modified on two devices before syncing, the system resolves the conflict automatically (last-write-wins by timestamp, or per-field merge where feasible) without silently discarding either side's changes.
- **Offline resilience**: Changes made while offline queue locally and sync automatically when connectivity resumes. No data is lost due to temporary network unavailability.

## Verification

- User registers a Cherry Studio account on Device A (Mac), logs in, creates an assistant named "Code Reviewer" with custom prompt, and adds a CherryIN provider with API key. User logs into the same account on Device B (Windows) - "Code Reviewer" assistant and CherryIN provider with API key appear automatically without manual import.
- User has conversation cloud sync disabled (default). User chats with "Code Reviewer" on Device A. On Device B, the assistant config is visible but the conversation history is empty. User enables conversation cloud sync on both devices - the conversation from Device A appears on Device B.
- User modifies the same assistant's system prompt on Device A (offline) and Device B simultaneously. When Device A reconnects, sync completes and the assistant retains one coherent version - no data silently disappears, and no duplicate assistants are created.
- User deploys the open-source sync server on their own VPS and configures the client to use `https://my-sync.example.com`. All sync features work identically to the official cloud - account login, incremental sync, conversation opt-in.
- User disables conversation cloud sync after previously enabling it. Existing cloud-stored conversations are retained (not deleted), but no new conversation data is uploaded. A separate "delete cloud conversations" action is available if the user wants to purge.
- User's network drops mid-sync. After reconnection, queued changes sync without user intervention and without duplicating or corrupting records.
- On the Passport web portal, user tops up credits and subscribes to cloud storage. The client reflects the updated quota immediately after next sync.
- User with 50,000+ messages across 200+ topics enables conversation cloud sync for the first time. Initial sync completes progressively (not blocking the UI) and the user can continue chatting during sync.

title: [Feature]: Agent Knowledge Base Tool - Enable Agents to Search RAG Knowledge Bases
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio has a fully functional Knowledge Base (RAG) system - users can create knowledge bases, index documents, and retrieve relevant chunks during conversations. However, this capability is only available through the Assistant workflow: an Assistant is manually assigned one or more knowledge bases in its settings, and retrieval happens implicitly during chat. Agents - which are far more capable at multi-step reasoning and tool orchestration - have no way to access the Knowledge Base at all. An Agent cannot search a user's indexed documents, cannot retrieve context from a knowledge base to answer questions, and cannot combine RAG results with other tool calls (e.g., OCR a document then search the knowledge base with the extracted text). Users who want RAG-powered answers must leave Agent mode entirely and use a manually configured Assistant instead.

## Goal

Agents can call the Knowledge Base as a first-class tool (`knowledge_search`) to query any of the user's knowledge bases and receive relevant document chunks with source citations - using the same retrieval pipeline that the Assistant workflow uses today.

## Spec

- A new Agent-callable tool `knowledge_search` is registered when the user has at least one knowledge base with indexed content. If no knowledge base exists or all are empty, the tool is not registered - Agents do not see it.
- The tool accepts a natural-language query and an optional knowledge base name/ID filter. When no filter is specified, the search runs across all knowledge bases the user has created.
- The tool returns ranked document chunks with: the matched text, a relevance score, the source document name, and the knowledge base name. The Agent uses these chunks as context to synthesize its response.
- The retrieval pipeline is identical to what the Assistant workflow uses - same embedding model, same vector search, same reranker (if configured). There is no separate retrieval path for Agents.
- Per-agent permissions apply: administrators can exclude `knowledge_search` from a specific Agent's allowed_tools, preventing that Agent from accessing the Knowledge Base even though the tool is globally available.
- The tool respects the user's existing Knowledge Base configuration (embedding model, chunk size, reranker settings) - no additional configuration is required to enable Agent access.

## Verification

- User has a knowledge base "Company Policies" with 20 indexed PDF documents. In an Agent conversation, user asks "what is our refund policy?" - Agent calls `knowledge_search` with the query, receives 3-5 relevant chunks from the policy documents, and synthesizes an answer citing the source document names.
- User has two knowledge bases: "Engineering Docs" and "HR Handbook". User asks the Agent "search HR Handbook for the parental leave policy" - Agent calls `knowledge_search` with the knowledge base filter set to "HR Handbook", and results come exclusively from that knowledge base.
- User asks the Agent "search my knowledge base for deployment procedures" but has no knowledge bases created - Agent does not attempt to call `knowledge_search` (the tool is not in its tool list) and responds that no knowledge base is available.
- Agent chains tools: user uploads a scanned contract image and says "find related clauses in my legal knowledge base". Agent calls `ocr_recognize` to extract text from the image, then calls `knowledge_search` with the extracted text as query - two tool calls in sequence, no manual intervention.
- Admin creates Agent "Public Bot" with allowed_tools excluding `knowledge_search`. Public Bot cannot search any knowledge base - the tool does not appear in its available tools, even though the user has knowledge bases with content.
- User changes the embedding model in Knowledge Base settings and re-indexes. The next Agent `knowledge_search` call uses the updated embeddings - no separate configuration needed for the Agent path.

However, `npx` is actually installed and available from both Command Prompt and PowerShell. The MCP server starts correctly if the command is changed from `npx` to `npx.cmd`. This seems to be a Windows command resolution issue when launching MCP servers. ### Context - OS: Windows 11 - Node.js: 24.15.0 - npm/npx: installed and available in PATH - Shell tests pass in both Command Prompt and PowerShell cmd: ``` C:\Users\xiaoy>node -v v24.15.0 C:\Users\xiaoy>npx -v 11.12.1 C:\Users\xiaoy>where npx D:\nodejs\npx D:\nodejs\npx.cmd ``` pwsh: ``` Get-Command npx -All CommandType Name Version Source ----------- ---- ------- ------ ExternalScript npx.ps1 D:\nodejs\npx.ps1 Application npx.cmd 0.0.0.0 D:\nodejs\npx.cmd Application npx 0.0.0.0 D:\nodejs\npx ``` So npx is clearly installed and available in PATH. Try to start or save/test the MCP server. 6. title: Tabs/AssistantItem: factor click + context menus from a single descriptor
body:
## Background

After PR #12060 (context-menu migration), `src/renderer/src/pages/home/Tabs/components/AssistantItem.tsx` maintains **two parallel menu trees**:

- A click-triggered \"more actions\" Dropdown still uses `antd Dropdown` (lines ~110-326).
- A right-click ContextMenu uses `@cherrystudio/ui` `ContextMenu` (lines ~353-555).

Both menus expose the same actions (edit, copy, clear, save-to-agent, icon-type submenu, tag management, sort, delete) but the menu construction is duplicated ~90 lines apart. Adding or tweaking an item requires editing both branches; tag operations could silently diverge between left-click and right-click.

PR #12060 took this as an acceptable follow-up because `@cherrystudio/ui` does not yet ship a click-driven dropdown menu primitive (only `ContextMenu` and `SelectDropdown`). Once a click-driven dropdown menu lands in `@cherrystudio/ui`, AssistantItem (and similar files: `AgentItem.tsx`, `AssistantPresetCard.tsx`, `YamlFrontMatterNodeView.tsx`) should drop the antd Dropdown.

## Proposed

1. Add a `DropdownMenu` primitive in `packages/ui/src/components/primitives/` (Radix `react-dropdown-menu` based, mirroring the structure of the new `ContextMenu`).
2. Factor a single \"menu descriptor\" array in `AssistantItem` (e.g. `{ key, label, icon, onSelect, danger?, children? }[]`) and render it twice - once from the click button, once from the right-click wrapper.
3. Do the same in `AgentItem.tsx`, `AssistantPresetCard.tsx`, and `YamlFrontMatterNodeView.tsx`.

## Why this matters

- Removes ~90 LOC of duplicated menu construction per file.
- Eliminates the silent-drift risk between click and right-click menus.
- Continues the v2 push to remove antd from the renderer surface.

## Out of scope for this issue

The legacy renderer CSS vars flagged by `comment-legacy-css-vars` in #12060's diff - tracked separately by the bot's reminder.

title: fix(agents): cron task sessions should use task name instead of agent name
body:
## Bug Description

When a CherryClaw agent runs scheduled cron tasks, all sessions created are named after the agent (e.g. MyBot) rather than the individual task name (e.g. Daily Report). Users cannot tell which session belongs to which task.

## Root Cause

In SchedulerService.ts, runTask() calls createSession with an empty object, so the session inherits the agent name.

## Proposed Fix

Pass the task name to createSession. One-line change:
  - createSession(agentId, {})
  + createSession(agentId, { name: task.name })

task.name is already populated from ScheduledTaskEntity.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a CherryClaw agent named MyBot
2. Add multiple scheduled tasks (Daily Report, Weather Alert)
3. Wait for tasks to execute
4. All sessions show as MyBot, indistinguishable

## Expected Behavior

Each session should be named after its task (e.g. Daily Report).

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.5

### Bug Description

Cherry Studio crashes unexpectedly multiple times per day. The app runs normally for hours, then quits without any warning or error dialog. This has been happening consistently for at least several weeks across multiple versions.

After analyzing the macOS crash report, the crash is:
- **Exception type**: `EXC_BREAKPOINT` / `SIGTRAP`
- **Faulting thread**: Thread 0 (main thread)
- **Root cause**: V8 engine internal assertion failure (CHECK/DCHECK), **not** an out-of-memory or null pointer dereference

The crash happens during the Cocoa RunLoop idle callback on the main thread. V8's garbage collector (`cppgc`) and JIT compilation optimizer are running in the background when a Rust native addon (via `cxxbridge`) appears to corrupt V8's internal object state, causing V8 to deliberately abort the process.

This is distinct from other reported crashes (#13578 which is OOM from large images, #7805 which is selection-hook null pointer).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch Cherry Studio and use it normally throughout the day (Agent conversations, MCP tools, etc.)
2. The app typically runs 10-15 hours before crashing
3. Crash occurs during idle moments - not triggered by a specific user action
4. No error dialog appears; the app simply disappears from the Dock

The crash is not consistently reproducible with a short series of steps. It appears to be a cumulative issue (GC pressure or memory fragmentation building up over hours of runtime).

### Expected Behavior

The app should not crash during normal use, even after extended runtime.

### Relevant Log Output

Key frames from the faulting thread (Thread 0) call stack:

```
Exception Type:  EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
Termination:     Trace/BPT trap: 5

Thread 0 Crashed (main thread):
  cxxbridge1$rust_vec$bool$capacity
  node::inspector::protocol::Target::Metainfo::version
  v8::Name::GetIdentityHash()
  node::PrincipalRealm::tick_callback_function() const
  cppgc::subtle::DisallowGarbageCollectionScope::~DisallowGarbageCollectionScope()
  v8::internal::OptimizingCompileInputQueue::Prioritize(...)
  v8::Exception::TypeError(...)
  __CFRUNLOOP_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_A_SOURCE0_PERFORM_FUNCTION__
  __CFRunLoopDoSource0
  __CFRunLoopDoSources0
  __CFRunLoopRun
  _CFRunLoopRunSpecificWithOptions
  NSApplication run
```

**Analysis summary**:
- V8 engine modules: 206 symbol references
- Node.js modules: 69 symbol references
- Total threads at crash: ~70 (high, with extensive mach_msg / IPC activity)
- The crash occurs when V8's cppgc garbage collector finds inconsistent state during a Rust cxxbridge interaction in the inspector/debugger protocol context

Full crash report (`.ips` JSON) can be provided privately if needed - it has been withheld from public posting to avoid exposing device identifiers.

### Additional Context

- macOS version: 26.4.1 (25E253)
- Device: Apple Silicon (ARM-64)
- This crash pattern has persisted across multiple Cherry Studio versions
- Restarting the app daily (~every 12 hours) works as a temporary workaround, which further supports the "cumulative GC pressure" hypothesis
- Related but not identical: #13578, #14248, #14600

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.5

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

This is somewhat adjacent to #14895, but the key point here is different: Knowledge Base embeddings could run directly inside Cherry Studio, with the app handling model download, caching, and inference, instead of requiring a separate embedding service.

### Desired Solution

I would like to suggest adding an in-app local embedding option for the Knowledge Base feature.

For example: Knowledge Base -> Embedding Model -> Built-in Local Embedding

The idea is that Cherry Studio could handle the embedding model download, local caching, and local inference inside the app itself, instead of requiring users to run a separate embedding service just for embeddings.

For many beginners, embedding configuration is one of the easiest places to get stuck when setting up a local Knowledge Base. Users may already know how to configure a chat model, but embeddings introduce another layer of concepts and setup:
- Which provider or model should I choose?
- Why can't I see any embedding models in the Knowledge Base selector?
- Why does this model not work even though I marked it as an embedding model?

A good reference is the Obsidian plugin Smart Connections. It provides local embedding inside the app environment. By default, it uses TaylorAI/bge-micro-v2. Smart Connections downloads and caches the model through Transformers.js, then runs embedding inference locally inside the app environment. From my own testing, this kind of setup works smoothly on a normal PC and does not require an advanced GPU. For ordinary note/document embedding, the resource usage feels quite reasonable.

This seems practical to implement because much of the hard work, such as model loading, caching, and local inference, is already handled by libraries like Transformers.js. Cherry Studio could start with a small default embedding model and keep the existing provider-based embedding options available for users who need more control.

The main goal is to provide a beginner-friendly path:
- Create a Knowledge Base
- Select Built-in Local Embedding
- Let Cherry Studio handle the embedding model locally
- No separate embedding service required

### Alternative Solutions

The current approach is to use external embedding providers or local model services such as Ollama, LM Studio, or cloud embedding APIs.

These options are useful for advanced users, but they still require extra setup. For beginners, having to install, configure, and keep another service running just for embeddings can make the Knowledge Base feature feel much harder than necessary.

Improving documentation for external embedding providers would help, but it would not fully solve the setup barrier. A lightweight in-app local embedding option would make the first-time Knowledge Base experience much smoother.

### Additional Information

Reference implementation:

https://github.com/brianpetro/jsbrains/blob/main/smart-embed-model/adapters/transformers.js

The Smart Connections implementation is useful as a reference because it shows a simple in-app local embedding path:

- Load Transformers.js inside the app environment
- Download a small embedding model
- Cache the model locally
- Run feature extraction locally
- Use the generated embeddings for local semantic search

The important part is not the exact model or exact backend, but the user experience:
- The app manages and runs the embedding model itself.
- The user does not need to start a separate embedding server.

Because this approach can run on top of the Chromium runtime using WebGPU when available and WASM when needed, it can be efficient on ordinary PCs and relatively easy to deploy across platforms.

The feature request is mainly about reducing the Knowledge Base setup barrier by adding an app-managed local embedding option. This could be introduced as a lightweight default option while keeping the existing provider-based embedding configuration for advanced users.

title: [Bug]: MCP tool response silently drops content when structuredContent is present
body: ### Issue Checklist - [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem. - [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881). - [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found. - [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc. - [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio. ### Platform Windows ### Version 1.9.5 ### Bug Description ## MCP tool `read_file` response silently drops `content` array when `structuredContent` is present **Client:** Cherry Studio 1.9.5 **MCP Server:** `@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander` (Desktop Commander) **Environment:** Windows 10, agent running as AI model via Cherry Studio ### Problem When calling the `read_file` tool from Desktop Commander, neither the AI model nor the user receives the actual file content. The AI only sees a tiny metadata object, and the user sees nothing in the chat UI. ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Configure Cherry Studio with Desktop Commander MCP server (`@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander`) 2. Call the `read_file` tool with a path to any plain text file (e.g. `read_file({ path: "/tmp/test.txt" })`) 3. Observe the tool result - the AI receives only: ```json {"fileName":"test.txt","filePath":"/tmp/test.txt","fileType":"text"} ``` 4. The actual file content is not visible to the AI, nor displayed to the user in the chat ### Expected Behavior The AI should receive the file content as a `type: "text"` item in the `content` array, and/or the user should see the file text rendered in the chat UI. At minimum, the data should not be silently lost. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell ``` ### Additional Context ### Investigation We traced the issue by examining the Desktop Commander source code on GitHub (`src/handlers/filesystem-handlers.ts`). **`handleReadFile` returns BOTH fields** (lines 122-138): ```typescript // For all other files, return as text. return { content: [{ type: "text", text: textContent }], // file content here structuredContent: { // metadata here fileName: path.basename(resolvedFilePath), filePath: resolvedFilePath, fileType, }, }; ``` **`handleReadMultipleFiles` returns ONLY `content`** (no `structuredContent`): ```typescript return { content: contentItems }; ``` When we called the sibling tool `read_multiple_files` on the same file, the AI received the full content correctly - confirming the server works fine. The only difference is the presence of `structuredContent` in the response. ### Root Cause The MCP `CallToolResult` has two fields: - **`content`** (array of `ContentItem`) - the primary response payload, intended for the model/AI - **`structuredContent`** (optional JSON object) - an extension field designed for client-side UI widgets (file previews, interactive tables, etc.) When Desktop Commander's `read_file` returns both `content` (with the actual file text) and `structuredContent` (with file metadata), Cherry Studio appears to either: 1. **Give precedence to `structuredContent`**, using it as the sole tool result for the AI and discarding the `content` array entirely, OR 2. **Fail to render `content` items to the user** when `structuredContent` is present, treating them as mutually exclusive The file data is present in the server's response but never reaches either the AI's context or the user's view - it is silently lost. ### Evidence That the Server Response Is Correct Other MCP clients handle this pattern correctly: - **VS Code GitHub Copilot**: shows both `content` and `structuredContent` in the tool output view ([vscode issue #297669](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/297669): "When tools return both content and structuredContent, output shows both") - **Google ADK**: passes the entire response (both fields) to the LLM context ([adk-python discussion #3893](https://github.com/google/adk-python/discussions/3893)) - **Claude Desktop**: renders `content` in the chat UI and uses `structuredContent` for the Desktop Commander file preview widget The MCP specification requires `content` to always be present. The `structuredContent` field is additive - it should not replace or suppress `content`. ### Workaround For Desktop-commander `read_multiple_files` (even for single files) instead of `read_file`, since it returns only `content` without `structuredContent` and works correctly in Cherry Studio. _Examined with AI assistance_

I searched existing issues and found some related discussions about plugin systems, CLI plugins, and pluggable capability systems, but I did not find an issue specifically about one-click model provider installation / authorization-based model service setup / provider configuration update.

Cherry Studio already supports custom model services, but users still need to manually enter the API key, Base URL, model IDs, and enable the provider. This flow works, but it can still be difficult for non-technical users and may easily lead to configuration mistakes. It also creates friction for third-party model service providers that want to offer a smoother onboarding experience.

I would like Cherry Studio to provide a model provider installation/update mechanism. This could be implemented through a plugin mechanism, provider install link, deep link, configuration import, or another suitable approach.

The user is redirected to the provider website to log in, authorize, activate the service, or create credentials.
After authorization is completed, the provider returns to Cherry Studio through a deep link, callback, or configuration import flow.
Cherry Studio shows a confirmation page before applying the change, including information such as the provider name, Base URL, model list, and permission scope.
After the user confirms, Cherry Studio automatically creates or updates the model provider configuration, adds or updates the model list, and enables the provider.
Cherry Studio optionally runs a connectivity check.

This mechanism does not need Cherry Studio to implement complex token lifecycle management. If the credential expires, becomes invalid, or needs to be reissued by the provider, the user can start the authorization flow again from the provider website. Cherry Studio only needs to support safely overwriting or updating the same provider configuration after user confirmation.

This feature would lower the barrier for users to configure model services and allow third-party providers to offer a more stable, secure, and maintainable onboarding experience. title: feat: Mise-based tool manager - build bundling, service, IPC, preferences, UI, tests
body:
## Parent

#15181

## What to build

A complete mise-based tool management system for Cherry Studio. Mise is bundled at build time and used at runtime to download/install CLI tools into `~/.cherrystudio/bin/`. The tool list is stored in the Preference system (`feature.mise.tools`). A `MiseService` lifecycle service reconciles on startup, and IPC channels allow the renderer to install/remove/query tools. A settings UI lets users manage their tool list.

### End-to-end behavior

1. **Build time**: `download-mise-binary.js` fetches the mise binary for the target platform and places it in `resources/binaries/{platform}-{arch}/mise`. `before-pack.js` invokes this and filters out non-target binaries.

2. **App startup**: `MiseService` (Phase.Background) locates the bundled mise binary, reads `feature.mise.tools` from preferences, and reconciles - installing any tools not already at the target version. Mise runs in an isolated environment under `~/.cherrystudio/mise/` to avoid conflicts with the user's own mise.

3. **Runtime IPC**: Renderer can call `mise:reconcile`, `mise:install-tool`, `mise:remove-tool`, `mise:get-state` to manage tools dynamically.

4. **Settings UI**: A tool manager page in settings where users can view installed tools and their versions, add new tools (name + mise tool key + optional version), remove tools, and trigger reinstalls.

5. **Preload**: Expose mise IPC channels through the preload bridge so the renderer can access them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mise binary is downloaded at build time for all supported platforms (darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, win32-x64)
- [ ] `MiseService` starts in Background phase, finds bundled mise, reconciles tool list from preferences
- [ ] Mise runs in isolated env (`~/.cherrystudio/mise/`) - does not read/write user's own mise config
- [ ] Tools are installed to `~/.cherrystudio/bin/` and tracked in `~/.cherrystudio/mise/state.json`
- [ ] Cache hit: tools at correct version are skipped during reconcile
- [ ] IPC channels work: reconcile, install single tool, remove tool, get state
- [ ] `feature.mise.tools` preference (type `MiseTool[]`) is defined and accessible via `usePreference`
- [ ] Preload bridge exposes mise IPC channels to renderer
- [ ] Settings UI page for managing tools (list, add, remove, version display)
- [ ] Unit tests for MiseService (reconcile logic, state management, env isolation)
- [ ] Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

When switching between models with different thinking/reasoning-effort support, the assistant-level `reasoning_effort` value can be overwritten by fallback logic and the original model's preference is lost.

Example: Model A supports thinking control and the user selects `none` (no thinking). After switching to Model B, the app applies a fallback reasoning effort for Model B. When switching back to Model A, Model A's previous `none` preference is no longer restored because the single assistant-level value was overwritten by Model B's fallback.

This changes the user's thinking preference unexpectedly and can affect request parameters, latency, and cost.

5. Switch back to Model A.
6. Observe that Model A's previous `none` / no-thinking preference is not preserved.

## Expected Behavior

Each model should preserve its own reasoning-effort preference independently. Switching to another model and applying fallback for that model should not overwrite the original model's stored preference.

If per-model persistence is not implemented, fallback should at least avoid destroying the previous model's user-selected value.

N/A

Root cause appears to be that `reasoning_effort` is stored as a single assistant-level value. Model-switch fallback updates that single value, so returning to the previous model uses the fallback value instead of the previous model-specific preference.

body:
